title: Unequal work
lesson: Equal request counts can hide unequal work; route new calls using current outstanding work while existing queued calls retain their assignment.
limitations: Illustrative two-worker, one-slot-per-worker schedule with perfect visibility; not a production benchmark.
Least request compares the two visible candidates; it is not an exact Envoy implementation or a universal improvement guarantee.
Existing requests are neither migrated nor retried; progress bars do not predict remaining time.
Audio levels, waveform timing and spectrogram were analysed; physical listening was not performed.
Self-reviewed by gpt-6-astra; no comparative recommendation against other model cuts.

transcript.text: In this illustrative agent tool service, round robin sends a short call to worker A and then worker B. Each worker has one execution slot; both calls complete.
A receives long call L1 while B receives short call Q3. Both workers have received two calls, but B finishes and becomes idle while A is still running.
Round robin sends Q4 to A. It waits behind L1 although worker B is idle. Equal turns do not account for different task durations.

The example switches to least-request routing for new calls. Q5 and then Q6 go to B, breaking the alternating pattern. A still has L1 running and Q4 waiting; the policy change does not move those calls.
L1 finishes on A. Q4 then leaves its local queue, runs on A, and completes. Both workers finish, with three calls assigned to A and four to B. The resolved scene holds, then fades to black.
